_README: One entry per input that was corrected after publication. Each entry names the SUPERSEDED
value, the REPAIRED value, and the provenance of the correction. The detector reports every
occurrence of a superseded value in a tracked file that is not accompanied by a repair marker.
TO ADD AN ENTRY: you have corrected a number that was already published. Add it here in the
same commit that lands the correction. That is the whole discipline; everything else is
THIS FILE IS THE SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE and that is deliberate and declared. Before this
instrument, finding a stale figure depended on whoever happened to read the right document.
Now it depends on whoever lands a correction remembering to file a row. That is strictly
better and it is not nothing.
`patterns` are Python regexes matched against a single line. `also_matches_repaired` must be
false for a pattern that would ALSO match the repaired value -- otherwise every repaired site

entries.title: eps_spec budget: 2e-4 superseded by 2e-2
entries.why: the budget row is calibrated under the branch-(iii) reading its own source document proves cannot close Step 6, and reads F(eps) < 1/6 -- a necessary condition at the MAXIMUM possible slack -- as a calibration point. Under the recommended repair the calibration is the eps at which mg-3ce3's `survives` predicate first fails: 0 RED / 6681 posets up to eps = 0.20, hence eps_leak ~ 0.20 and eps_spec <= 0.2^2/2 = 2e-2.
entries.standing_instruction: docs/state-history/attempt-mg-88bd.md:98 -- "do not carry 2x10^-4 or the n ~ 10^5 crossover as flat text"

entries.title: eps_leak read-off: 0.02 superseded by 0.20
entries.direction: the stale value INFLATES PESSIMISM (it is the square root of the budget error)
entries.why: same root cause as eps_spec_budget; this is the input the square is taken of.

entries.title: remaining gap factor: ~5e3 superseded by ~50
entries.corrected_by: mg-e35c F5 (derived); struck in the primary doc by mg-5827
entries.direction: the stale value INFLATES PESSIMISM 100x -- THIS IS THE NUMBER THAT TELLS A READER HOW FAR THE WALL IS
entries.why: the gap factor is 1 / eps_spec up to the constant, so it moves with the budget: 1/2e-2 ~ 50, not 1/2e-4 ~ 5000.

entries.title: master-bound RHS constant: 3.3e-5 superseded by 3.3e-3
entries.why: the RHS is eps_spec/6 * n^2, so it carries the budget error verbatim.

entries.title: (LIB)/(LIB-const) crossover: n ~ 1e5 superseded by n ~ 900
entries.direction: the stale value OVERSTATES the range in which the weaker form is numerically harder -- it makes 'every plausible range' look true when it is OVERSTATED
entries.why: the crossover is (C/gamma)/(eps_spec/6), which moves 100x with the budget: 3C/3.3e-3 ~ 900.

entries.title: Claim 7.2 threshold: n <= 100 superseded by n <= 10 (primitive: n <= 100)
entries.direction: TWO ERRORS IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: the input is 100x too pessimistic, and the claim is weaker than the available argument (primitivity gives n <= 2/eps_spec). Do not report this one as a simple inflation.
entries.why: eps_spec * C(n,2) >= 1 requires n(n-1) >= 100 at the repaired budget, i.e. n >= 11.

authorities.why: carries the standing instruction and both values; this is where the correction is RECORDED. Flagging it would be flagging the fix.
the audit that PERFORMED the correction. Its occurrences of the superseded value are the refutation itself.

this instrument. The registry must name the superseded value in order to search for it; a detector that flags its own registry reports a defect on every run and is therefore useless. DECLARED, not hidden -- see README section 'the exclusions'.

_frozen_note: Committed transcripts under code/ are EVIDENCE AT A COMMIT, not live claims. They record what
an instrument printed on the day it ran, and repairing them would destroy the record. They are
reported in a SEPARATE bucket -- FROZEN -- which is informational and does not fail the gate.
This is a real weakening of the gate and it is declared: a live claim that happens to live
under code/ (a README asserting a figure in the present tense, say) will be under-reported.
Markdown files directly under code/*/README.md are therefore NOT treated as frozen.
